title: Evidence to Execution v7: Secure Outcome-Hidden Simulation Practice for U.S. Equities

lessons.title: Confirm the course boundary and prerequisite skills
lessons.objective: State the simulation-only U.S.-equity scope, identify work this curriculum does not cover, and demonstrate the number, unit, source, and risk-per-share skills needed for later lessons.

sections.title: Read number and unit together
sections.body: A dollar amount, share quantity, price, percentage, and timestamp are different facts. Keep the unit beside every number. A ticket that changes from dollars to shares has changed the instruction.
sections.prompt: A ticket shows Quantity: 25 and Unit: shares. What does 25 mean?

check.success: The unit controls the meaning of the number.
check.correction: Read the number and its unit as one field.

sections.title: Use the correct course boundary
sections.body: This course is simulation-only and focuses on U.S. listed stocks and exchange-traded funds in U.S. brokerage accounts. It does not teach options, futures, forex, cryptoassets, taxes, non-U.S. rules, live signals, or personalized security recommendations. Current broker documents control whenever they differ from a lesson example.

sections.title: Check basic risk arithmetic
sections.body: For a long simulation with a $20.00 planned entry and a $19.60 invalidation, technical risk is $0.40 per share. If the execution allowance is $0.05, planned risk is $0.45 per share. A $18 loss boundary allows 40 whole shares after rounding down.
sections.prompt: Which quantity stays within an $18 boundary at $0.45 planned risk per share?

check.success: Forty shares plan $18.00 of risk.
check.correction: Divide the loss boundary by planned risk per share and round down.

sections.title: Read a quote and a ticket without guessing
sections.body: Use DIAG-01 in the learner case bank. Record the quote timestamp, bid, ask, spread, ticket quantity, unit, side, order type, session, and time in force. Mark any missing field unknown.
sections.prompt: What should happen when the ticket unit is hidden?

options: Infer shares from the last trade
Stop and reveal the unit before continuing
check.success: A hidden unit is a blocking ambiguity.
check.correction: Do not test an unclear ticket with an order. Reveal and read the field.

sections.title: Choose the correct route after the diagnostic
sections.body: Use DIAG-02. If number-unit reading or risk-per-share arithmetic is wrong, complete the supplied prerequisite worksheet before Lesson 1. If the scope statement is misunderstood, reread it and explain the excluded markets in your own words.
sections.prompt: Does passing this diagnostic mean the learner is ready for live trading?
sections.answer: No. It only confirms entry skills for a simulation curriculum. Live-trading readiness is outside the course claim.

sections.title: Keep the claim narrow
sections.body: I will use fictional or historical simulation data, verify current broker rules, and treat course completion as evidence of practice rather than permission to trade live.

mastery_criteria: States the U.S.-listed-equity and ETF simulation scope
Reads numbers together with their units and timestamps
Calculates technical and planned risk per share
Routes a failed prerequisite check to remediation

mastery_standard.remediation: Preserve the failed diagnostic, complete the prerequisite worksheet, pass V7-DIAG-R, and then take unopened V7-DIAG-T2. Never repeat an opened transfer form.

lessons.title: Build the evidence timeline before judging the trade
lessons.objective: Given fixed orders, fills, notes, and chart records, build a source-labeled timeline, reconcile position state, and mark unsupported claims unknown before judging the decision.

sections.title: Sort four kinds of evidence
sections.body: Observed means a source states it directly. Calculated means it follows from recorded facts. Reported means a timestamped note states the learner’s intent. Unknown means the record cannot support the claim.
sections.prompt: A broker export shows a buy fill at 10:01:14 and a sell fill at 10:02:07. Which claim is calculated rather than observed?

options: The holding interval was about 53 seconds
The learner intended a breakout entry
The stop was below the prior candle
check.success: Elapsed time is calculated from two observed timestamps.
check.correction: Use observed only for facts shown directly. A time interval derived from timestamps is calculated.

sections.title: Use a six-event evidence clock
sections.body: Record context captured, trigger recorded, order submitted, fill received, exit condition recorded, and exit filled. Write unknown when an event is missing. Do not fill gaps with later price action.

sections.title: Rebuild position state one fill at a time
sections.body: A $100 buy request receives 2 shares at $30 and 1 share at $31. The supported position is 3 shares at a $30.33 weighted-average price before fees. The request amount remains separate from executed quantity.
sections.prompt: What is the supported position after both fills?

options: $100 of exposure with no known quantity
check.success: You used executed quantities and weighted prices.
check.correction: Position state comes from fills, not the original dollar request.

sections.title: Preserve cancellations and open positions
sections.body: A record shows a buy fill and a later canceled sell order, with no closing fill. Record the remaining open quantity, the canceled instruction, and the missing closing evidence.
sections.prompt: What does the canceled sell prove?

options: The order did not remain active
The last quote became the exit price
check.success: A cancellation is an order-status fact, not an execution.
check.correction: Never treat a canceled order as a fill.

sections.title: Keep conflicting clocks visible
sections.body: A screen recording and broker export disagree by five seconds. Keep both timestamps with source labels. Use only the ordering each source can support until a shared clock or third source resolves the conflict.
sections.prompt: Why should both timestamps remain in the record?
sections.answer: The conflict is evidence about capture quality. Removing one timestamp would hide uncertainty and could make the trade look more orderly than the source supports.

lessons.title: Check cash and settlement before the setup
lessons.objective: Given a dated U.S. cash-account ledger, separate settled cash, unsettled proceeds, and held deposits, then decide whether a purchase is supported without guessing.

sections.title: Name the funding source
sections.body: Before reviewing a setup, identify settled cash, unsettled sale proceeds, deposits still on hold, and any payment deadline shown by the broker.
sections.prompt: Which balance is safest to treat as immediately available for a new cash-account purchase?

options: Expected proceeds from a future sale
Settled cash shown as available to trade
check.success: Settled cash is the clearest supported funding source.
check.correction: Do not treat account value or expected proceeds as settled cash.

sections.title: Use T+1 as a starting point, not a complete answer
sections.body: Most U.S. stock and ETF trades settle on the next business day. Settlement alone does not answer every cash-account question. A purchase paid with unsettled proceeds and then sold before the purchase is fully paid may create a good-faith violation; buying and selling before paying can create freeriding. Use the dated broker ledger and current firm notice rather than memorizing labels from an example.

sections.title: Separate purchase funding from later proceeds
sections.body: A cash account starts with $800 settled cash and buys $600 of stock. A second purchase that same day would use proceeds from a different sale that have not settled. The first purchase has a stated funding source. The second sequence needs a dated settlement check before it can count as eligible.
sections.prompt: What is the correct process response to the second purchase?

options: Verify the current settlement path and wait if funding is unclear
Assume every same-day sale makes cash immediately settled
Use margin rules in the cash account
Ignore settlement because the trade is small
check.success: Unclear funding fails closed until verified.
check.correction: Trade size does not remove cash-account payment and settlement constraints.

sections.title: Build a cash-account ledger
sections.body: For each event, record trade date, expected settlement date, settled cash before the event, purchase amount, sale proceeds, deposits on hold, and the broker message. Do not merge settled and unsettled balances.

sections.title: Handle a holiday and a deposit hold
sections.body: A sale occurs before a market holiday, and a recent bank transfer is still on hold. Recalculate the timeline using the broker’s dated settlement and deposit information. If either source is missing, mark the next purchase ineligible.
sections.prompt: Which rule should the learner memorize?

options: All sale proceeds settle at midnight
Verify the dated settlement and hold information for the actual account
Cash-account restrictions never apply after a sale
check.success: The reliable habit is current, account-specific verification.
check.correction: Calendar and deposit details can change the usable-funds timeline.

lessons.title: Verify margin, intraday rules, and personal suitability
lessons.objective: Use current broker documents to identify the applicable intraday margin method, calculate a sample deficit, and separate account permission from personal loss capacity and suitability.

sections.title: List the questions margin adds
sections.body: Record the account’s equity and buying power. Then record the maintenance rule, any stricter house rule, the interest rate, what happens after a deficit, and whether the firm has adopted the new intraday standard.
sections.prompt: Which source controls the account decision today?

options: The current rule plus the specific firm’s dated implementation and house policy
check.success: Current firm implementation and house rules must be verified.
check.correction: Do not assume a past framework or another firm’s controls apply.

sections.title: Treat 2026 as a transition period
sections.body: FINRA’s new intraday margin standards became effective June 4, 2026, with a firm implementation period ending October 20, 2027. During the transition, identify the broker’s method, effective date, house requirements, intraday margin calculation, and response to a deficit. Do not apply the former pattern-day-trader shortcut unless the current firm document still says it applies to that account.

sections.title: Separate buying power from loss capacity
sections.body: A broker screen allows $8,000 of intraday exposure, but the learner’s written maximum planned loss is $40 and essential funds are excluded. A second example shows required intraday margin of $1,200 against $1,000 available, creating a $200 deficit under the stated example method. Permission, margin capacity, deficit handling, and personal loss capacity are separate checks.
sections.prompt: What does displayed buying power prove?

options: The maximum loss is limited to the deposit
The broker may accept that exposure under current controls
check.success: Buying power is an account-control fact, not proof of safety or edge.
check.correction: Leverage can increase losses and may lead to liquidation.

sections.title: Build a margin rule card
sections.body: Save the firm and account type. Add the policy link or document date, current rule, stricter house rule, borrowing cost, deficit response, forced-sale rights, and the support channel used to answer any open question.

sections.title: Make suitability explicit
sections.body: List essential bills, emergency savings, debt, experience, and risk tolerance. Ask whether a large loss would harm a near-term need. If the money is needed for living costs or comes from consumer debt, the decision is no live trading.
sections.prompt: Which response is safest when the planned funds are needed for rent next month?

options: Keep the activity simulated and protect essential funds
Use margin so less cash is tied up
check.success: Essential funds should not be exposed to day-trading risk.
check.correction: Liquidity and smaller size do not make essential funds suitable for speculation.

lessons.title: Verify broker, session, and fractional-share behavior
lessons.objective: Read a broker ticket from number through time in force, verify firm-specific session and fractional-share rules, and fail closed when policy sources conflict.

sections.title: Read number and unit together
sections.body: Read the number and unit together every time. A ticket can express dollars, whole shares, or fractional shares. After a partial fill, use the actual open quantity—not the original request—to plan a close.
sections.prompt: What is missing from “Sell 10”?

options: The unit and the position context
check.success: The number is unsafe without its unit and position context.
check.correction: A ticket must be read as a complete instruction.

sections.title: Fractional behavior is firm specific
sections.body: Verify eligible securities, sessions, order types, minimums, execution timing, aggregation, price treatment, voting or dividend treatment when relevant, transfer limits, and how residual fractions are liquidated. Do not assume whole-share behavior applies.

sections.title: Close the actual position, not the original request
sections.body: A $100 buy produces 3.217 shares. A later sell ticket defaults to dollars. To close the position, the learner must confirm the current share quantity, the sell unit, and the broker’s fractional sell rules.
sections.prompt: Which ticket evidence matters most?

options: The current executed share position and sell unit
check.success: Closing quantity comes from the current position and ticket unit.
check.correction: The original request does not define the remaining share position.

sections.title: Create a broker behavior checklist
sections.body: Use a two-pass readback. Basic pass: symbol, side, quantity, and unit. Full eight-field pass: symbol, side, quantity, unit, order type and price fields, session, time in force, and estimated effect. Then verify fractional-share support, eligible order types, extended-hours limits, cancellation behavior, and how exact-position closing works.

sections.title: Handle a policy-page conflict
sections.body: The ticket allows a selection that an older help page says is unavailable. Save both sources, check their dates, use current in-app disclosures or firm support to reconcile the conflict, and fail closed until resolved.
sections.prompt: What should the learner do first?

options: Assume the ticket guarantees the behavior
Preserve both sources and verify the current policy
check.success: Conflicting broker evidence requires dated reconciliation.
check.correction: Changing order type does not resolve an unknown ticket rule.

lessons.title: Set the loss boundary and exposure before size
lessons.objective: Calculate whole-share size from maximum planned loss, invalidation distance, and execution allowance, then apply remaining session and correlated-exposure limits before accepting quantity.

sections.title: Write risk inputs before quantity
sections.body: Record maximum dollar risk, planned entry, structural invalidation, total adverse execution allowance, side, and existing exposure. Buying power is checked later.
sections.prompt: Which value must be set first?

check.correction: Starting from shares or buying power can make risk expand to fit the trade.

sections.title: Define the execution allowance clearly
sections.body: State whether the allowance covers adverse entry, adverse exit, or the total expected execution gap. Use one convention consistently so the same slippage is not omitted or counted twice.

sections.title: Calculate and round down
sections.body: Long example: planned entry $25.00, invalidation $24.60, total adverse execution allowance $0.05, and maximum risk $45. Risk per share is $0.45. Quantity is floor($45 ÷ $0.45) = 100 shares.
sections.prompt: What quantity keeps planned risk at or below $45?

check.success: One hundred shares uses the full $45 boundary without exceeding it.
check.correction: Add the execution allowance to the structural distance, then round down.

sections.title: Accept zero as a valid answer
sections.body: If one share would exceed the maximum risk, or if the invalidation cannot be defined, the correct quantity is zero. Do not widen the stop or hide execution cost to force eligibility.

sections.title: Check combined and correlated exposure
sections.body: Example: a $50 session boundary has $25 already committed to a highly related position. A new short has $0.49 planned risk per share. Only $25 remains, so the size cap is floor($25 ÷ $0.49) = 51 shares, not the 61 shares allowed by a separate $30 trade limit. State the chosen grouping rule before the session; correlation is a risk-control assumption, not a precise live statistic.

check.success: The portfolio and session limits constrain each new position.
check.correction: Per-trade compliance does not override combined exposure.

lessons.title: Make the setup pass a calibrated eligibility gate
lessons.objective: Build a simultaneous eligibility gate with units, sources, baselines, and missing-data rules, then apply it consistently to passing, borderline, and failing cases.

sections.title: Separate context from permission
sections.body: Fast movement and high volume describe context. They do not by themselves permit entry. Permission comes from a written trigger, invalidation, and all required gates passing together.
sections.prompt: Which statement is an observable trigger?

sections.body: Every threshold needs a unit, dated source, development sample, baseline, review date, and missing-data rule. Do not copy a threshold to a different symbol, session, volatility regime, or broker without new evidence.

sections.body: Worked calibration: over 20 development observations, acceptable regular-hours examples had quote age at or below 2 seconds, spread at or below 0.15% of midpoint, and visible size at or above 800 shares. options: Yes, because the trigger is the main signal
Only after a market order preview
No, all required gates must still pass
check.success: Eligibility is the intersection of all required gates.

lessons.title: Test the playbook before trusting the setup
lessons.objective: Write a frozen strategy test protocol, include execution costs, separate development from evaluation data, and report sample uncertainty without presenting a small result as proof.

sections.title: Name the evidence a playbook needs
sections.body: A strategy claim needs a written rule. It also needs a market and session, a test window, exclusions, a result measure, costs, data checks, and a separate set of evaluation cases.
sections.prompt: Which statement is a testable hypothesis?

options: In regular hours, cases meeting rules A through D will be evaluated over the next 10 bars after stated costs
check.success: The statement defines conditions, window, and evaluation.
check.correction: A hypothesis must be specific enough to reproduce and disconfirm.

sections.title: Separate development from evaluation
sections.body: Use one group of cases to build the rule. Use a different group to evaluate it. If the rule changes after those results are seen, those cases are no longer a fair evaluation. A new evaluation group is needed.

sections.title: Include friction before judging expectancy
sections.body: Use DEMO-V7-TEST-A in the case bank. It supplies a small table with gross R, spread cost, slippage, and fees. Compute net R for each observation, then report count, win rate, mean, median, range, and the number of rule violations. A positive mean in a small sample is a hypothesis, not validation.
sections.prompt: What should be reported?

options: The gross result proves an edge
The tested sample was negative after stated costs
check.success: Report the bounded result with its assumptions.
check.correction: Do not overgeneralize or delete inconvenient observations.

sections.title: Write exclusions before looking
sections.body: Before viewing evaluation outcomes, lock the setup definition, data source, inclusion and exclusion rules, cost model, missing-data rule, metrics, and stopping point. Record every rule variant tried. Selecting the best result from many variants without adjustment is a form of backtest overfitting.

sections.title: Treat small samples as hypotheses

State the decision the test must support, the variability, the number of tried rule variants, and an uncertainty interval appropriate to the measure. Increase size while confidence is high
The small sample is suggestive but insufficient; keep the rules fixed and test more independent cases

lessons.objective: Choose among market, limit, stop, stop-limit, wait, and cancel by comparing the price, non-fill, trigger, gap, partial-fill, and cancellation failures the plan can tolerate.

sections.body: A rapid series of attempts proves frequency and timing. It does not prove revenge, fear, or greed unless the learner recorded those states. Review behavior neutrally and ask what current evidence supported each attempt.

options: Three entries occurred within six minutes
The last loss caused the next trade
check.success: The timing and count are observed; motive requires evidence.
check.correction: Do not diagnose emotion from sequence alone.

sections.title: Use a reset that fits the learner and risk level
sections.body: Define observable reset triggers before the session. Examples: two required fields omitted, the same rule reread three times without a clear answer, two serious rule violations, an unreconciled order, uncertain position state, or a preset planned-loss boundary. A serious violation is one that bypasses a risk, eligibility, account, or position-state control—not any ordinary mistake.

sections.title: Let the earliest stop condition control
sections.body: The session policy ends execution after the daily loss boundary, two serious rule violations, degraded attention, unreliable data, or platform failure. Two rule violations occur before a later profitable trade. The session ended at the second violation.

check.success: A preset stop is not renegotiated by outcome.

lessons.objective: Given deficient and strong fictional process artifacts, accurately score the artifact with observable anchors, use NS only for missing evidence, separate outcome from process, and write a neutral correction. The learner is scored on review accuracy—not on the fictional trader’s original score.

sections.title: Keep process and outcome on separate lines
sections.body: A profitable trade can have weak evidence or poor adherence. A losing trade can follow a sound, prewritten process. Score the decision before using the outcome for context.
sections.prompt: Which classification is possible?

options: Strong process with a losing outcome
check.success: Process and outcome are independent dimensions.
check.correction: Do not let P&L determine the process score.

sections.title: Use observable 0–3 anchors
sections.body: Use the rubric in templates/process-review-rubric.md. Evidence: 0 no sources; 1 incomplete or late; 2 complete and timely; 3 resolves conflicts without hindsight. Account/readiness: 0 unchecked; 1 partial; 2 all required gates checked; 3 handles a changed constraint. Playbook/eligibility: 0 absent; 1 vague; 2 calibrated gates applied; 3 transfers without copying thresholds. Risk: 0 missing or exceeds a limit; 1 incomplete inputs; 2 correct and rounded down; 3 applies combined limits. Plan: 0 post-hoc; 1 missing fields; 2 complete before ticket; 3 cancels when a premise changes. Execution: 0 unsupported; 1 names an order only; 2 matches failure mode; 3 handles partial fill or gap. Behavior/review: 0 outcome-led or contaminated; 1 vague; 2 neutral and artifact-cited; 3 tests a correction later. Use not scorable when the required artifact does not exist.

sections.title: Score a winner with missing evidence
sections.body: A trade profits, but no trigger or invalidation was saved. Evidence and plan quality are level 0 or not scorable. Outcome is positive. The correction is to lock those fields before the next case, not to praise the result as proof.

sections.title: Write one neutral correction
sections.body: Use this form: “On the next case, before reveal, I will [observable action] so that [specific evidence gap] is closed.” Avoid labels such as careless, bad trader, or always.

sections.title: Do not overlearn from a short sample
sections.body: A pattern across three cases is a hypothesis. Record the count, contexts, and uncertainty. Test the correction on later cases before changing the full playbook.

options: Before the next reveal, save the spread limit and quote timestamp

sections.title: Recall the full chain
sections.body: Evidence and data readiness; account and broker rules; playbook evidence; risk; eligibility; decision card; order failure; reset or session stop; process review.
sections.prompt: Which step occurs before position size?

check.success: Risk inputs and invalidation come before quantity.
check.correction: The workflow prevents size and outcome from leading the decision.

sections.title: Use pause, plan, reveal, review
sections.body: Pause at a fixed timestamp. Lock the evidence and decision. Reveal a fixed interval. Compare the later record with the untouched plan. No clicks, live orders, or post-reveal edits are permitted.

sections.title: Watch one model case
sections.body: Open GUIDE-01 in the neutral key-free packet released by the facilitator and follow the facilitator walkthrough. The case fails because the quote is stale and the spread exceeds its calibrated gate. The completed decision is WAIT. Later price movement does not repair the pre-reveal data and execution failures.
sections.prompt: How should the model be scored?

options: Correct process if the saved gates supported wait
Profitable because the move was predicted
check.success: A supported wait is a complete decision.
check.correction: Outcome does not override the pre-reveal evidence.

sections.title: Walk through GUIDE-01
sections.body: Use the supplied learner packet, response template, reveal window, and facilitator key. The facilitator may model where to find evidence and how to cite it. GUIDE-01 is a demonstration and does not count as independent mastery.

sections.title: Complete coached case GUIDE-02
sections.body: Use the changed symbol, session, and partial-fill conditions in GUIDE-02. The coach may identify a missing field but may not provide a value or decision. Lock the response before reveal.
sections.prompt: What should remain unchanged?

check.success: The workflow transfers; market inputs are rebuilt.
check.correction: Do not copy prices, thresholds, or outcomes between cases.

sections.title: Lock both artifacts
sections.body: Each case must have a stable case ID, timestamp, original evidence record, original decision card, fixed reveal window, rubric scores with artifact citations, and one correction.

sections.title: Route one weak dimension
sections.body: Choose the lowest rubric dimension and return to its specific lesson. Complete one bounded repair; do not repeat the whole curriculum.

sections.title: Depth before speed
sections.body: I will complete two careful no-click cases, including a supported wait or no trade, before moving to independent assessment.

lessons.title: Complete the independent no-click capstone
lessons.objective: Across three dates, complete a balanced fixed-reveal simulation blueprint: one valid proceed, one valid wait, one valid no-trade short decision, one operational stop, and one delayed transfer case. Preserve originals and earn facilitator-scored evidence only on dimensions the case actually supplies.

sections.title: State the assessment rules
sections.body: Cases must be selected without outcome knowledge. The timestamp and reveal window are fixed. The original response remains unchanged. Every rubric score cites an artifact. Profit and prediction accuracy do not determine mastery.
sections.prompt: Which action invalidates a capstone case?

check.success: Post-reveal editing destroys the independent evidence.
check.correction: Preserve the original response and route the gap forward.

sections.title: Use four cases over at least two dates
sections.body: Session A uses V7-CAP-A and V7-CAP-B. Session B, on a later date, uses V7-CAP-C and V7-CAP-D. Each session includes setup, two cases, and scoring. The four packets vary direction, session, liquidity, account constraint, data quality, and operational risk. At least one correct decision is wait or no trade.

sections.title: Inspect the artifact checklist, not a solved case
sections.body: Use templates/case-response.md and templates/process-review-rubric.md. Required artifacts are listed, but no answer values appear in the learner packet. The facilitator key stays separate until every response in the session is locked.

sections.title: Complete cases V7-CAP-A and V7-CAP-B
sections.body: Session A: complete V7-CAP-A and V7-CAP-B from the learner bank. Allow 16 minutes per case and 8 minutes for setup and artifact checks. Stop if data, platform, order, or position state becomes unreliable.

sections.title: Change the operating context
sections.body: One case must use a different session or account constraint. One must contain a partial-fill, halt, stale-data, or borrow complication. Rebuild all affected fields.
sections.prompt: What is required when context changes?

options: Rebuild market-specific and account-specific values while preserving the workflow
check.success: Transfer means stable process with rebuilt inputs.
check.correction: Do not reuse stale thresholds or execution assumptions.

sections.title: Complete cases V7-CAP-C and V7-CAP-D later
sections.body: Session B: on a later date, complete V7-CAP-C and V7-CAP-D without the model or coaching. Allow 16 minutes per case and 13 minutes for scoring and remediation routing. Keep all four originals and separate revisions.

sections.title: Apply the mastery rubric
sections.body: A case passes when all required artifacts exist, no post-reveal editing occurred, risk and stop rules were followed, and the facilitator score reaches level 2 on every applicable dimension. Not scorable is honest but does not satisfy a required capstone dimension. Three of four cases must pass, including at least one supported wait or no-trade decision.
sections.prompt: What does not count toward mastery?

options: A profitable case whose plan was edited after reveal
A losing case with strong process
A case with an honest not-scorable dimension
check.success: Outcome cannot rescue contaminated assessment evidence.
check.correction: Mastery depends on locked evidence and process, not profit.

sections.title: Preserve evidence, then decide what comes next
sections.body: I will use capstone results to choose targeted practice. I will not treat completion, simulated profit, or self-entered case counts as permission for live trading.

mastery_criteria: Completes four outcome-hidden cases across at least two dates
Preserves stable case IDs and untouched pre-reveal artifacts
Includes at least one supported wait or no trade
Transfers the workflow across changed market, account, and execution conditions
Cites evidence for every rubric score and routes weak dimensions

No specific case ID is mandatory. Replace any failed or exposed form with an unopened active v7 equivalent or a validated generated parallel form.
